line: Living your truth, whatever that means to you, is the only way to access your real abilities, willpower, strength and creativity. We can't live somebody else's truth: we don't even know it, though too often we guess it

Too often we base so much of our choices on what someone else thinks, or what we think they'll think: a spouse, parents, kids, friends, coworkers. That path leads not just to less happiness but to less power

It's like driving with your foot on the gas and the brake at the same time: basically nowhere, on a real rough ride. Living what's true for you individually is the only way to get your foot off the brake; on the gas, looking ahead, you make a hell of a lot more progress

An encouragement for today: think about what in your life is maybe not in alignment with who you truly are, a job, a relationship your heart isn't in anymore, personal habits and lifestyles not really in alignment with who you truly know you are, friends with a negative impact, and how it's impacting you. Maybe you already know deep down. The moment you align it with who you are and what you desire, your power and speed towards the life you want are truly unleashed; while it stays out of line, you're never going to access your real power

Out of alignment, resistance within us gains incredible power over us. Brave enough to change and live in a way that feels true and right to you, regardless of what anybody thinks, you flip the tables and gain incredible power over him
Too often we give too many fucks away to other people. Stop giving a fuck what people think: what do you think, who are you, what do you really want? With one life to live, that's what matters
Beyond happiness, your ability to create, build, grow and progress is directly linked with your alignment with who you truly are: the more you discover and follow it, the greater the power
Don't wait for the power, mood or strength to make the change: make it, and your power will grow exponentially
Love is what it's all about: not about not loving others, but about loving yourself enough to do what you know is right for you

Make some kind of decision today: everybody can live more in alignment, more of who we are and less of who we think somebody wants us to be. Be what you really want, without waiting for someone to say it's okay, and "you will kick more ass than you can possibly imagine"

Kegels are exercises of the pelvic floor muscles, and they seem to get nowhere near enough talk among men and in men's health circles. Strengthening that whole area makes a tremendous difference in your sex life, absolutely, and in so many ways it really boosts sort of your core energy and life force
Three keys: consistency, focus on the rear, and both Kegels and reverse Kegels

Consistency: you only see a benefit if you do them on a regular basis. A couple of times a week, "oh, I should do some Kegels for a minute", and you might as well not even worry about it. Like anything else in life, the real benefit comes when you do it every day: make it a daily routine. **Story:** tally marks, in an app called Tally App on the phone, track the most important daily habits, and they're great for the do-it-one-to-five-times-a-day kind of things

Focus on the rear: different ways of doing Kegels have dramatically different impacts, especially on your sex life. Three muscles are involved: the bulbocavernosus (BC), the pubococcygeus (PC) and the iliococcygeus (IC). The technical names don't really matter: what matters is where they sit and which you focus on

Going from the front to the back, and up as you go back: the BC is the most in front, kind of under your balls; the PC is in the middle; the IC sits further back, against the coccyx bone, so when you squeeze it you can almost feel it in your super low back

Focusing forward, on the PC and especially the BC, is much less effective for controlling your arousal level, with a much different impact on your sex life than the deeper, rear muscles. Personally found: the deeper and more towards the back, the bigger the muscles, with greater control; the smaller BC and PC a lot of times don't give that ability, and without the biggest, most powerful muscles, the IC towards the rear, you don't get the same impact

So, highly suggested: still imagine stopping the flow of urine, or holding in a fart, but feel the squeeze towards the back, against the coccyx bone in your super low back, the ideal place. That gives much greater control over your arousal, and sort of a bigger life energy impact than the BC, just under your nuts

Both Kegels and reverse Kegels: reverse Kegels are incredibly impactful for the overall health of the pelvic floor, and really, really impactful for your sex life. Kegels strengthen the pelvic floor, for better control, stronger orgasms and more life force energy; mixing in reverse Kegels gives much more control over your arousal level. If one part of Kegels helps you last longer in bed more than anything else, it's reverse Kegels. Do at least as many reverse Kegels as Kegels

A reverse Kegel squeezes the same muscles the other way, ideally again towards the rear, though you really want to exercise all of them: imagine pushing out a fart or peeing harder. Mixing both is a whole different world from Kegels alone, a huge difference
If you haven't been doing Kegels, you will be truly amazed at what just a week or two of consistent practice can do for the way you feel, and definitely for your sex life

Kegels seem super important for all men, a topic to keep talking about, and other men hopefully will too, as they really improve a number of aspects of your life. However good your sex life is now, probably all of us could use even more and better there. But it's not just sexual performance: your sex energy and the strength of these muscles feed into your life force energy, your physical energy for other physical stuff and your drive, and many aspects of us are impacted

A recommended app: Stamena, used on an iPhone, with probably an Android version too. Essentially a timer meant for Kegel practice, it beeps and takes you through both Kegels and reverse Kegels in progressively more challenging routines. App or not, definitely do Kegels, lots of them, and you will feel the power

Every 24-hour period holds 96 15-minute blocks, and 1/96th of the day can change your life, and is changing it, for better or for worse. Too often we look at the big, huge task and everything it will take, and let that stop us from doing the thing: repairing a relationship, getting fit, eating better, building a business, being a better father. Mentally trying to reach the place of having accomplished the whole thing makes it seem huge

That's not the best way to look at it, and not how it works: we live life a moment at a time, really, not a project at a time. But we need some sort of period we can attack and really make changes in: 15 minutes, or thereabouts

In 15 minutes you might work your body (every day, and you're way more fit), drive to the liquor store for beer, have real communication with your spouse, or get lost on social media. The really good, powerful things can be knocked out 15 minutes at a time, at least, and what negatively affects us is those short periods too, sometimes the ones that don't happen, like 15 minutes of real communication with your spouse every day. That's where all of the change lies, where your power lies

A strong belief in being present, and in meditating to practice presence, since that seems to be where we're most effective and also most joyful: a moment-by-moment thing. But planning or eliminating an activity, creating or eliminating a habit, takes a little more than a moment. "15 minutes you can change your life. 15 minutes you are changing your life"

Jerking off daily probably takes less than 15 minutes; to the point of ejaculation, in kind of a negative way where you lose that energy, almost guaranteed probably less. Set a timer: your only job for those 15 minutes is to eliminate it. Day after day, your internal power and fire completely change. You don't have to do it all at once

Set a timer: if your relationship with your spouse could use improving, set one in the other room, and when it goes off, immediately walk over and talk for 15 minutes, not forcing conversation if it's not the right time. It doesn't have to be six hours, or the whole project, or getting all the way fit, building the whole business or fixing the whole relationship at once. 15 minutes at a time, every day, will change your life in more powerful ways than you can possibly imagine. For a relationship, the most important thing is probably communicating, planned every day: call that person, or talk to your spouse about what has kind of come up in the last few days, or "I've been feeling this, or I see maybe you're feeling that". Real communication will do amazing things

"We are the things that we do every day." It doesn't take a lot of time, but it takes an intention. A negative activity probably happens at the same time every day: when it's about to start, set a timer and just don't do it for 15 minutes
If you don't sleep well, maybe set a timer 15 minutes before bed and wind down in the most effective ways you can figure out, learn and grow with over time

For nutrition, maybe 15 minutes at the start of the day in the kitchen, seeing what you have and strategizing the fuel that will fuel you effectively and what to buy at the store. Decide in your mind how you'll fuel your body today and more often than not you'll follow through, if not every single time then a pretty good chunk of the time, and change your life and your body. It might take only 45 seconds, but at first maybe you do need the timer, with pen and paper if that's how you roll, or your phone. Strategizing instead of winging it throughout the day gets dramatically different results

For a business, you don't have to build it all at once. Determine the daily activities that make it happen and do them for 15 minutes. If that's all the time you have, or you're not feeling it, fine: 15 minutes every day of whatever feels like the most important thing for that area of your life
For fitness, if you're not in the shape you want, it does not take a lot of time. Set a timer for 15 minutes and go, every day, and you will see changes, without a doubt
The number one thing that matters more than anything else for your fitness is intensity: there are lots of ways to feel better and lots of physical tools, but above all else, just get intense

Don't make it a big thing of "intense workouts all the time forever". 15 minutes, set a timer, go as hard as you can: "That's your only job forever." The next day, the same again, at home, at the gym, wherever
It doesn't take a lot: we have to break stuff into smaller chunks so we can take action, both to add awesomeness to your life and to get rid of things

Rolling over onto your phone in bed, checking email and all this stuff first thing, kind of sucks and does crappy things to our brain. Right after we wake up our minds are really open and receptive, so the start of your day guides your mind for the day

If your days aren't going the way you want, look at what you do the first 15 minutes, for the next three weeks, to get that habit in place: on waking, set a 15-minute timer on your phone labeled something like "15 minutes of focus", and it clicks you into how-can-I-start-my-day-effectively mode

Maybe meditate for five of those minutes, do push-ups for a couple, take a cold shower for a couple, or roll over and love on your spouse for a few: however you can ideally design your day, in your unique way
Focus on something for 15 minutes. "It's 1% of the day." Everything will change
Meditation has a direct and powerful link not only to your physical state and sex drive, but also to your performance and enjoyment of sex itself, in four ways
Stress: meditation destroys stress, and stress destroys sex drive

Stress puts the body into fight or flight mode, where things like sex drive are basically shut down and take a back seat to surviving: the state cavemen were in defending against an animal. Today it's work, relationships, whatever stress weighs on us. The more stress, the more sex drive feels the effects

Meditation is without question one of the most powerful, if not the most powerful, ways to reduce stress, with countless studies and science on its effects on cortisol and stress hormones, so much proven data

To the extent we reduce stress, we improve sex drive: it's just the way our bodies work, a direct inverse relationship. Less stress, and the more you feel like having sex, the better you focus, the more present you are, the better you perform and the more you enjoy it. Better for life, and certainly for your sex life
Hormones: tremendous physical benefits on a hormonal level. Less stress means less cortisol and related stress hormones, and meditation also improves the hormones we want

One really important hormone, among those meditation improves, is DHEA, also referred to as kind of the grandmother hormone. It acts on its own, but also produces lots of downstream hormones, including testosterone for men and estrogen for women

DHEA is really closely linked to aging: levels gradually decline as we age, and doctors use it as one of the markers of sort of the true age of your body, versus your birth certificate. Higher DHEA, more youth

Meditators were studied and found to have higher DHEA levels than non-meditators by as much as 40%: a huge, drastic impact on actual hormone levels. It's not just about a clear mind, concentration or presence: there are really dramatic physical benefits to mind and body
More DHEA not only increases youth, it also tends to increase sex drive, because it's converted into downstream hormones like testosterone
Endorphins: a lot of people don't really associate them with meditation

A lot of people know endorphins are released with exercise, as in a runner's high, and make us feel incredibly good. They also lead to a lot of sort of mind and physical state conducive to a positive sex drive and sex experience
Meditation boosts them too: one study in the Biological Psychology Journal in 1995, "so it's been a while", studied elite runners and meditators and found very similar endorphin-boosting effects
Endorphins make you feel awesome, put you more in the mood for sex and more able to enjoy it, with really powerful physiological effects on your body and mental and physical state
Presence: without question, meditation helps your ability to be present, with a focused, quiet mind

One of the other big things that kills sex drive, and especially your sex life and ability to perform and enjoy, is your ability to be present. If you're mentally distracted and your mind is always somewhere else, you're never going to be in the moment anywhere near the same way. It affects performance and enjoyment, and when constant throughout the day, your sex drive too

The more you get comfortable with your mind and step back, not caught up in all the clouds running around but chilling in the blue sky above them, the more you can be in the moment with sex, your sex energy and your sex life
With a more focused and quiet mind you're simply a better lover: you last longer, you're more attentive, you enjoy sex better and you're more able to control your arousal level
Meditation has really powerful benefits in so many aspects of life, and one of them is most definitely your sex life

If you haven't started a practice, personally, the favorite app is Headspace, "Can't recommend that highly enough"; the first 10 days are free. Of course there's more than one way to meditate: however you do it, definitely meditate, starting Monday morning

What matters more than anything is happiness, yours and what you bring others: "that's the only thing that matters", that and making memories. Stuff, being in shape, a good sex life, awesome kids, the trappings of the modern world are nice, but nothing else matters but your happiness

Miserable in a job that pays for your lifestyle, or unhappy in a relationship you're not brave enough to end: is that pursuing happiness in a way that feels true on the deepest level? Maybe not. Knocking out a job, relationship or habit that isn't contributing to our happiness sometimes takes bravery

Happiness is not easy: long-term happiness is not doing whatever feels good in the moment, and a lot of times it's the opposite. Sleeping in and sitting around all day might feel good in the moment, but leaves you feeling worse and worse the longer you do it; not facing what you need to face in a relationship leaves you more and more unhappy; job hunting or building a business to escape an unhappy job might not feel good, but it's what long-term happiness takes

Happiness is the measure, the ultimate measure of any alpha male, not the stuff, the people you know or the money. Only you know, within your own life and mind, how to be the most happy and bring the most happiness to others

Part of why we're here, and seemingly a huge role of our job as men: bringing happiness to those we love, our family, which sometimes means the hard short-term thing. If they're missing the hell out of you because you're gone all the time at a job you hate, do something about it. Miserable because you're out of shape? Prioritize your long-term happiness

The more true joy lies behind something, most often the more resistance you'll face getting to it. Either we accept facing resistance over and over and move towards that thing anyway, or we let it stand in the way and die with regret. Be brave
**Story:** years, in so many different areas, were spent unhappy from not being willing to face resistance and pursue happiness

Happiness doesn't just happen. We choose to be happy kind of moment to moment, it seems: no matter how bad things are, we can always kind of choose our attitude. Long-term happiness is up to us too: choosing a path that creates happiness for us and others, the only thing we'll take with us

You could die where you stand, in the fractions of a second after getting hit by a bus. Pursuing our true happiness, as the guidepost and measure of our path, is the way to a life without regret. Deep joy comes a lot of times from harder short-term choices that aren't necessarily the easy choice

We all, it seems, have some aspect of our life we know inherently we truly want to change, for a different level of joy and satisfaction for us and maybe those around us, but we let resistance stand in the way. Choose happiness, and go after whatever is eating at you

The 15 minutes talked about a couple of days ago: every day, 15 minutes toward what will bring the greatest increase in joy for you and those around you, like submitting job applications, planning and building your own business, or setting a timer to talk and figure stuff out in a relationship
Really fit but miserable? Who cares. In fitness, a job or a relationship, "quote unquote success" without true happiness on a deep core level is failure, not success

You have more resistance-facing power than you've ever felt before. Today, take some positive step in an area of your life where you haven't been: figure out what holds you back from the most happiness and get after changing it

A nootropic is basically anything that's really a cognitive enhancer, enhancing brain power. Technically there are a couple of qualifications, but any cognitive enhancer is generally called that. Four, grown to love over the years, made a meaningful difference in the brain personally, and "I'll bet" they can in yours too

All four are essentially natural. Some drugs enhance the brain too, like a class called racetams, quite common in various forms, especially as you dig online into the world of nootropics, but sticking with natural solutions is highly recommended. **Story:** racetams and other synthetic nootropics were tried; they seem to suffer from what synthetic forms usually do: natural forms are simply much better for us and tend to work better with our bodies
The four: Huperzine A, Alpha GPC, acetyl-L-carnitine and ginkgo biloba

Huperzine A, extracted from moss. It basically boosts acetylcholine in the brain, a very key neurotransmitter that directly impacts brain capacity: learning capacity, memory, processing speed, reaction time. Instead of being a source of choline, it stops choline's breakdown, keeping it active, so it effectively raises our levels
Personally, incredible benefits taken first thing in the morning. Really cheap, works really well: highly recommended
Very tiny doses, measured in micrograms, not milligrams: the recommended dose is anywhere between 50 and 150 micrograms a day; try that and see how you feel

It's often in a lot of brain-boosting blends, and often way overdosed: four or five hundred micrograms stuck in one is just too much. Various dosages were tried, and as with a lot of things in life, more is not necessarily better, definitely with huperzine. Really not a fan of supplement blends in general, for a lot of reasons, and this highlights it: get it directly. Easy to get, all over Amazon, quality brands in local health food stores; very cheap and very effective

Alpha GPC, alpha glycerophosphocholine, kind of the sister supplement to Huperzine A. Huperzine A improves choline levels in the brain, and actually the body, by inhibiting its breakdown; Alpha GPC is a direct source of choline, which turns into acetylcholine, kind of the downstream form, the actual neurotransmitter. The combination is really powerful for brain and body
Like lots of neurotransmitters, choline isn't just used in the brain but throughout the body, with a lot of benefits for both

A lot of studies show improved power output and physical performance in athletes. Exercise drops choline levels, and Alpha GPC prevents those exercise-induced reductions. Taking choline prior to a workout, the power output difference personally felt is amazing; you'll feel it in your brain the rest of the day, and certainly in your workout
For Alpha GPC, quite a few good brands; a favorite is the NOW brand, available all over and taken on a regular basis, along with others
It's isolated from a food, from a couple of sources including soy. Not a big fan of soy, but it's such an isolated substance, without soy proteins, that it seems not a big deal

The preferred dosage of most of the studies is 600 milligrams. Personally, 600 milligrams usually twice a day; maybe once a day might be good for you, depending on your volume of physical activity. When that's pretty high, twice a day before your workouts seems really the ideal time

It takes a little longer to take effect as a pre-workout: take it a good hour and a half or two hours before the workout, and have your coffee or whatever, say, 15 minutes before, since those work a lot more quickly

Acetyl-L-carnitine, covered in an episode on energy, absolutely improves energy, but most definitely the brain too. Basically a mitochondrial-boosting supplement: mitochondria, essentially the powerhouse of our cells, are in almost every cell and especially dense in brain cells, so boosting them boosts energy overall and in the brain
One of fasting's amazing benefits is the mitochondria boost, which happens especially after we break the fast, one of its fundamental powerful effects

Carnitine is in all our cells, and you can buy just L-carnitine: look for the acetyl-L-carnitine form, which crosses the blood-brain barrier to act on the brain's mitochondria, improving cognition, learning, memory and mood

Acting on mitochondria everywhere, it also reduces fatigue, shows notable improvements in sperm quality in the studies (obviously your balls have mitochondria too) and improves muscular endurance: really wide-ranging benefits. A favorite, taken on a regular basis

Ginkgo biloba: really all four benefit the body in so many ways besides the brain. Ginkgo works by enhancing circulation, especially to the brain, but also the rest of the body; enhancing it so significantly to certain parts of the brain gives massive brain-boosting effects, specifically on memory

Personally, acetyl-L-carnitine, Alpha GPC and even huperzine definitely bring a lot of processing speed, reaction time and learning capacity; ginkgo, a significant difference in memory, and the studies are really strong around memory too

Hormone-boosting supplements need cycling; others like ginkgo don't necessarily: you could pretty much take it regularly forever and be fine, at a moderate, appropriate dose. **Story:** cycling off things occasionally anyway, partially for the benefit and the sort of fun of feeling them fresh and new again. Back on ginkgo after a break, more really vivid memories from the past would pop into the brain: the past kind of lit up

Beyond memory, the enhanced circulation helps lots of aspects of the brain, and the body: it enhances nitric oxide, really important for blood flow, including for erections and exercise performance, and oxygen uptake. Some studies even show significantly improved skin moisture, "I would imagine" because of circulation to the skin
Ginkgo is absolutely worth taking, especially as we get a little older: a memory all of a sudden better than it has been recently is awesome
Dose: around 120 milligrams one to three times a day. It typically comes in 60 or 120 milligram capsules, the dosage a lot of the studies and brands use
Take any or all of the four: they're all safe in appropriate doses, even at pretty high crazy doses, which you don't need, since more is not necessarily better
Timing of the four

Ginkgo is the only one of the four really recommended at night: before bed is another awesome time. It can be taken pretty much whenever; personally, three times a day, usually with each of the two cups of coffee mixed with supplements, and once again before bed
Some people take Huperzine A before bed, which will definitely bring more vivid dreams and potentially lucid dreaming; personally, it kind of works a little better earlier in the day
Alpha GPC and acetyl-L-carnitine: definitely recommended earlier in the day, first thing, then maybe midday or afternoon, whenever you have that second cup of coffee
Personally, these are the top four brain-boosting supplements ever found, after trying lots of others, the favorites: highly recommended to give them a shot
Sprinting is one of the very best ways to boost your hormonal profile as a man

Think primal: for optimizing hormones especially, it really helps, since much of our body and mind responds the way it would have in a primal time, not necessarily in today's world. As cavemen, sprinting meant chasing down a hunt or running from a predator, and our bodies got the message "I need to be a man right now": strength, power and the hormones to kill this bison or run away from this bear. So it just makes sense that sprinting at absolute maximum effort signals our hormones to boost, and they really do: modern science shows it in the numbers we can test

It's one of the most beneficial things you can add to your life, even with no other changes to your fitness, nutrition or anything else: just add it two or three times a week. It's amazing how little time it takes, so there's absolutely no excuse of not having time: you either put in the effort or you don't

Studies show as little as one six-second sprint of maximum effort raised human growth hormone levels for as much as 60 minutes after, and boosts testosterone as well. Not a lot of time, just the effort, and you'll really feel the benefits in your hormones, "I promise you"
How to do it

Start with individual sprints of at least six seconds. The recommendation if you're not sprinting now: five sprints of six seconds, 30 seconds in total, with, say, a 5 or 10 second break between. Two minutes or less, and you can make incredible changes in your testosterone and human growth hormone levels. Two or three times a week, "That's all it takes": less than 10 minutes a week for all the sprint workouts you need

Work up gradually in sprint length, eventually to maybe five 30-second sprints: still only two and a half minutes of running and maybe as much break, five minutes or less a couple of times a week, a pretty good routine with amazing results

The studies measured one six-second and one 30-second sprint. The six-second sprint raised both human growth hormone and testosterone, for at least 60 minutes after. The 30-second sprint raised human growth hormone by 450% more than the six-second one, and kept it elevated 90 to 120 minutes instead of 60. So definitely work up to sprints as long as 30 seconds. Beyond 30 seconds you're more than likely not really in a full all-out sprint, it seems, "Or if you are, then man, good on you"

Ideally you're outside, running. The personal favorite, and seemingly the ideal way: barefoot when possible, in a park, on the grass, which seems to put us in a solid biomechanical place with our running

In a shit ton of snow, or stuck in a hotel in the middle of the airport, an elliptical is a good backup: you can recreate sprinting pretty well on one. A little caution with a treadmill: you could try it, but absolute full speed, all-out on one seems a little sketchy. But ideally get outside, even for two minutes, even one
Go hardcore, absolutely all out, not a 60%, kind-of-running-fast

Depending on your fitness and flexibility, a few minutes to kind of warm up are suggested: some burpees, push-ups, jumping jacks, squats, or rolling out your legs with a massage roller. Be smart and don't pull a hamstring: walking out of the office on your lunch break after sitting all day and instantly bolting into a full hundred percent sprint is not recommended. Give at least a couple of minutes, depending on your condition, to loosen up the muscles

Get a sprint session in today and "I'll bet" you'll feel the difference tomorrow: probably better morning wood, that kind of energetic difference. The benefits will certainly compound over time on a regular basis
Do some today, right now: if you're listening, you have an extra 60 seconds or two minutes. Shut off the podcast two minutes early if you have to

Other benefits: it raises your metabolism, helps burn fat, and brings cardiovascular benefits. But the big reason all men should really be sprinting, it seems, is that it boosts hormones in really powerful ways, independent of any other changes. If you're already kind of kicking ass with fitness, nutrition and lifestyle, with hormones in great shape, you'll get an even further boost, feel even stronger and have even more human growth hormone and testosterone. Conversely, if you're not in a great place hormonally, for any number of reasons, just starting with sprinting will really give you a boost in getting your hormones back into a good place

Psychologically too: if it's been a while since you really sprinted, doing five, even six-second ones, brings an amazing mental and mood boost along with the hormonal boost. There's no damn excuse not to: literally a couple of minutes of effort, but you have to go hardcore

Your pain is your power: a fundamental truth that personally took a long time to learn, with a dramatic impact on our life. Wherever your greatest pain points are now, or have been in the past, that's the source of your strength: your challenges and pain make you stronger and make you who you are. In the midst of the pain it's not always easy to see: it's real easy to get overwhelmed and bummed out, and not see it for what it truly is, your strength

**Story:** why helping men feel great and kick ass is such a passion: a pretty typical childhood; never an athlete, just kind of a skinny little kid. After high school, a job, marrying pretty young, and filling what seems to have been a lack of true purpose with negative things on the outside. The diet got worse and worse, with no idea what was being done, and no care either: more and more weight, weaker and weaker, more and more hurting, more miserable mentally and emotionally

**Story:** there was a wife at the time, loved, and a daughter had pretty young (three amazing kids now), and parts of life were awesome, but being in such a shitty place internally and physically made it miserable. You've probably been there, "we've all been there", in some way, with sort of health, wellness and habits, not feeling good because of them

**Story:** by 25 it felt like twice that age: the heaviest and most out of shape ever, unable to run a quarter mile to save one's life, literally, falling apart, mind and body a mess. Some half-hearted attempts at change, but nothing ever really stuck

**Story:** then came one of the major events of a lifetime, which shifted things. Of the three kids, two girls and a boy, the son, Andrew, is in the middle. At nine days old he wasn't really seeming to do that great, wasn't eating a lot, and by the end of the day his lips were a shade blue, terrifying. At the Instacare his pulse oxygen was low; then the ER, and a couple of hours later the news: a couple of holes in his heart and what's called a narrowed aortic arch. He needed open heart surgery, and had it two days later

**Story:** the job then was stock trader at a financial services company, trading for clients, a typical corporate gig: pretty good money, but absolutely miserable, probably part of what fed a negative life experience in a lot of ways. The wife and kids were awesome, but the job was hated, the body in terrible shape, life physically miserable

**Story:** about the next three months were spent by his side in the ICU at the children's hospital, on a leave of absence from the stock trading job. So thankful, and so lucky to be near such amazing care: Andrew's surgeon, one of the top surgeons in the country, absolutely saved his life, and without him Andrew probably wouldn't be alive today
**Story:** without question the hardest time of life to that point, and it changed something
Galvanization: going through hard things makes us stronger, applying a force to produce a stronger outcome. It doesn't always feel like that, but it's true

**Story:** it unleashed a new determination to live the life wanted. Until then there was seemingly the idea a lot of us have kind of as kids: not really seeing the finite nature of life, seeming to feel we'll live forever. Now came the realization: you're going to die. Do you want to die like this, in this condition, living life this way? The answer was no. What had been stop-and-start, half-hearted efforts completely transformed, during that experience and the months after

**Story:** all that pain, so hard to deal with and like nothing dealt with before, needed somewhere to go: all the emotion, energy, sadness and heartache were poured into workouts, hill sprints at the time, literally crying while running them. It took years to really recognize what had been happening: all that pain and difficulty was coming on board as strength, a transformation into a stronger, better, more capable person who could attack and deal with life in a new way

Hard, difficult things not only give us the experience of having gone through them: they shift our perspective. Getting through them, you realize you're stronger than you think you are, and sometimes it takes those kinds of events to make you really realize it. **Story:** a divorce not that long ago, for a long time a worst-case scenario in the mind that couldn't even be imagined; it was hard, but going through the time with Andrew, and years and years later the divorce, brought that realization
Whatever pain you're experiencing, now or maybe in the past, serves a purpose: it builds you into the person you are
